slides.text: Near Berlin, 1898. Work began on Beelitz-Heilstatten, a sanatorium for tuberculosis patients.
It grew to about 60 buildings: one of the largest hospital complexes around Berlin.
In World War One it treated wounded soldiers. In 1916, one of them was a young corporal named Adolf Hitler.
In 1945 the Soviet army took it over. It stayed a Soviet military hospital until 1994.
In 1990, East Germany's fallen leader Erich Honecker stayed here, before he was flown to Moscow.
Then most of it was abandoned. Wards, stairwells, operating rooms... left to the forest.
Locals say it's haunted. Horror fans come from all over just to look at it.
Going inside the ruins is forbidden. But today a treetop walkway lets you look down on them.
